sentences.text: Crr/683/2024 on 13 September, 2024

Author: Suvra Ghosh
Bench: Suvra Ghosh
13.09.2024 jb.
jdt.
Crr No. 683 of 2024 (Cran 1 of 2024) In Re: Sri Vishal Jaiswal & Ors.
Mr. Aniruddha Bhattacharya Mr. Indranuz Dutta Ms. Benazir Sk.
...
For the Petitioners Faria Hossain Ms.Trina Mitra ...
For the State Re: CRAN 1 of 2024 Affidavit of service and supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the petitioners are taken on record.
None appears for the private opposite party despite service.
Heard learned counsels for the petitioners and the State.

Learned counsel for the petitioners seeks stay of the proceeding being Sessions Case no. 16(06) of 2019 pending before the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track,
2 nd Court, Sealdah, South 24 Parganas on the ground that the petitioners who are the members of the matrimonial family of the private opposite party have been falsely implicated.

entities.text:
Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track,
2 nd Court, Sealdah, South 24 Parganas
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Despite the fact there is no material against them under Sections 498A/307 of the Indian Penal Code, charge sheet has been submitted against them under Sections 498A/307/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code and their prayer for discharge from the case has been turned down by the learned trial Court vide order dated 11th December, 2023.

Learned counsel for the petitioners takes this Court to the statement of the doctor who treated the private opposite party and submits that though the alleged incident of assault appears to have occurred sometime in March, 2015 as stated in the FIR, the complaint was lodged on 8th October, 2016 and the prescription of the attending doctor was seized on 4 th November, 2016, the delay not being explained.

Per contra, learned counsel for the State submits that the learned trial Court was not able to consider framing of charge in the matter since the petitioners failed to appear before the Court on several occasions from 2019.

In an earlier revisional application filed by the petitioners on similar issues as the present application, being CRR 1557 of 2021, this Court, vide order passed on 11th April, 2023 observed upon consideration of the evidence collected and relied upon by the prosecution that no interference was called for at that stage.
The petitioners were granted liberty to canvass the points at the stage of consideration of charge or in course of trial.
Pursuant to the said order, the petitioners filed an application for discharge which was turned down by the order passed on 11th December, 2023.

Upon consideration of the submission made on behalf of the parties as well as the material on CRR/683/2024 on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7205650/
1 record, this Court is inclined to hold that the matter needs to be heard on merits.

Let the matter appear under the heading 'Contested Application' in the monthly list of November,
2024.

Further proceedings of Sessions Case no. 16(06) of 2019 pending before the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track, 2nd Court, Sealdah, South 24 Parganas qua the 2 nd petitioner and 5th petitioner be stayed till 30 th November, 2024 or until further orders, whichever is earlier.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track, 2nd Court, Sealdah, South 24 Parganas
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is made clear that the proceeding shall continue in so far the other petitioners are concerned and they should appear before the learned trial Court on the next date of hearing positively.

In default,
the learned trial Court shall be at liberty to take necessary steps, in accordance with law.
CRAN 1 of 2024 is disposed of.
Urgent certified website copy of this order, if applied for, be supplied to the parties upon compliance with all requisite formalities.
(Suvra Ghosh, J.)
